clue.text: Sloth disorientated composer

indicators.note: something disorientated has lost its bearings, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lazy creature has lost its way, and a composer is somehow involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disorientated' turns SLOTH into the English composer of The Planets.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst was an English composer, best known for The Planets suite.

clue.text: Leaves without difficulty

definitions.meaning: passes on to a successor, as in a will

explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath is to pass something down; winning easily is winning by an idiom from horse racing.

clue.text: Lottery offers winners excessive rewards initially — could be made this?

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A complaint that lottery prizes are far too big and ought to be reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the whole clue: the excessive rewards could be made smaller.
explanation.definitionFit: The question asks what the over-large prizes might be made: smaller, reduced in size.

clue.text: Maximum speed of boat, in the bow

parts.note: top means maximum, as in top speed
a knot is the unit of speed for ships, one nautical mile an hour

explanation.surface: A boat's top speed, measured at the front of the vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' is not the front of a ship but a ribbon tied in the hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A topknot is a ribbon bow or tuft of hair worn on top of the head.

clue.text: Put back in to control country

parts.note: a rein is what a rider uses to control a horse, and to rein is to control
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: Someone is restored to power so as to run the nation.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone to a former post is to put them back in it.

clue.text: When it's dry, fruit growing is unending

indicators.note: unending means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raising means growing, as crops

explanation.surface: In a drought, fruit cultivation never stops.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a grape that has been dried, so a fruit in its dry state.

clue.text: Relating differently, as a whole

indicators.note: differently means the letters of the preceding word are arranged another way

explanation.surface: Telling a story another way, seen in its entirety.
explanation.definitionFit: Integral describes something whole or complete, essential to the whole.

clue.text: Like dramatist, keep quiet about The Birds

parts.note: sh is the exclamation telling someone to keep quiet
avian means relating to birds

explanation.surface: A playwright's style involves staying silent about a play called The Birds.
explanation.walkthrough: The Birds is a play by Aristophanes, a red herring. 'about' is a link here. Shavian means of George Bernard Shaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Shavian describes things in the manner of George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright.

clue.text: From Welsh town, be removing guns

indicators.note: removing means the following letters are taken out of the town name

parts.note: Abertillery is a town in south Wales

explanation.surface: Weapons from a Welsh town are being taken away.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery is the heavy guns of an army.

clue.text: Wading bird showing grief leaving river at first

indicators.note: leaving means the river letter departs from the grief word
at first places the dropped letter at the front of the word

parts.note: regret is sorrow or grief

explanation.surface: A heron-like bird shows sorrow as it leaves the river.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron that wades in shallow water.

clue.text: Recent race covered in papers

parts.note: something recent is new
a sprint is a short fast race

explanation.surface: Reports of a fresh race fill the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covered in' is only a link here; the pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheap paper newspapers are printed on is the stuff the papers are made of.

clue.text: Agent abandoned by female, 19

indicators.note: the agent word is left behind by the letter for female, so that letter is dropped from it

parts.note: a factor is an agent who buys and sells for another

explanation.surface: A theatrical agent is dropped by a woman client.
explanation.walkthrough: '19' points to the answer of 19 across, PLAYER, which is the definition here.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor is a player on the stage, the sense of 19 across.

clue.text: Cutting flower-girl down to size, a shy person

definitions.meaning: read literally, a girl named after a flower is being reduced in size

explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a playful reading: Violet is a flower-girl's name, and cutting down to size is diminishing her.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a bashful person who shrinks from attention.

clue.text: Hold forth about new fancy

indicators.note: the speechifying word goes around the letter for new, enclosing it

parts.note: to hold forth is to orate, to speak at length

explanation.surface: Someone lectures at length about a fresh whim.
explanation.definitionFit: Fancy decoration is elaborate, the adjective sense of ornamented.

clue.text: As a baby-sitter, am insured after accident

indicators.note: after an accident things are mangled, so the letters of the words before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A childminder says she is covered by insurance following a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a woman employed to look after children.

clue.text: Pints are set out in lines for sailors

indicators.note: to set out is to lay out afresh, so the letters of the two words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: Glasses of beer are laid out in rows for a crew of seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges PINTS ARE. Sailors call the rope that ties up a small boat its painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A painter is a rope on a small boat's bow used for tying up, so painters are sailors' lines.

clue.text: Attacked without warning, knight reportedly used force to get in

indicators.note: reportedly means the title word is taken by how it sounds, not how it is spelt

parts.note: Sir is the title of a knight
prised means levered open with force

explanation.surface: A knight is said to have broken in by force in a surprise attack.
explanation.definitionFit: To be surprised is to be caught or attacked unexpectedly.

clue.text: Dissipated young girl shut up

parts.note: a miss is a young girl
pent means confined, shut up

explanation.surface: A wild young woman has been locked away.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is dissipated has been squandered or wasted.

clue.text: 'Grass" heard in ears, i.e. drug

indicators.note: heard means the informer word is taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a grass is British slang for an informer, also called a nark
otic means relating to the ears

explanation.surface: An informer is overheard whispering in someone's ear about drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' turns NARK (informer) into NARC, which sounds the same. 'Grass' and 'nark' are British slang for a police informer.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses or induces sleep.

clue.text: Catty author's marsupial

parts.note: T. S. Eliot wrote Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, so the cat author is a possum, abbreviated with an O

explanation.walkthrough: 'Catty' refers to cats, not spite: Eliot's pen name for his cat poems was Old Possum.
explanation.definitionFit: The American marsupial is often called simply a possum.

clue.text: One who performs better on piano

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another means it follows it

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a better is one who bets, and a layer is one who lays bets

explanation.surface: Someone plays the piano better than others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is not the comparative but one who bets: a layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is someone who performs, on a stage or an instrument.

clue.text: Plant used as fodder in canton

explanation.definitionFit: Lucerne is the British name for alfalfa, and also a Swiss canton and city.

clue.text: Row about doctor's deal

indicators.note: the row word goes around the doctor abbreviation

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A dispute over a doctor's business arrangement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is not an agreement but pine or fir wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Deal is sawn softwood, a kind of building lumber.

clue.text: Danger is over — there's no sea mist

definitions.meaning: an idiom for it being safe to proceed
read literally, the shoreline is not obscured by fog

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says nobody is watching and it is safe to go ahead, taken literally of a fog-free shore.

clue.text: Walk, for change, after public transport stops

indicators.note: after places the change letter behind the transport word

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
P, a penny, is small change

explanation.surface: Getting off at the tram stop and walking for a change.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk heavily or trek a long way.

clue.text: Remove camera's essential component

indicators.note: component means the answer is a part found within the following words

explanation.surface: Taking out a vital part from a camera.
explanation.definitionFit: To erase is to remove or wipe out.

clue.text: Get together in a state

parts.note: Mass is the short form of Massachusetts, a US state

explanation.surface: People gather somewhere in an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or collect things together.

clue.text: Make red and black tapestry in German town

indicators.note: the black and tapestry pieces are placed inside the town's name

parts.note: Ems (Bad Ems) is a spa town in Germany
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an arras is a wall tapestry, named after the French town

explanation.surface: A red and black wall hanging is displayed in a German town.
explanation.definitionFit: To embarrass someone is to make them blush, turning red in the face.

clue.text: Chap going round rotunda used to measure distance

indicators.note: the man's name encircles the building word, which ends up inside it

parts.note: Peter is a man's name, a chap
a rotunda is a round building with a dome

explanation.surface: A man walks around a domed building to gauge its distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedometer counts a walker's steps and so is an instrument for gauging distance walked.

clue.text: Workers taken in by leading journalist? That's correct

indicators.note: the workers are absorbed into the journalist's abbreviation

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the senior journalist
men are workers, as in a workforce

explanation.surface: Staff are employed by a top newspaper editor who confirms a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct its errors.
